lead: Ymbert de Damoise’s 370-franc funeral payment, 31 January 1371
status: Unresolved citation; not a verified primary craftsman link
detail: Wilson 2021 p 19 n 49 attributes a receipt for the funerals of Audrehem and Charny to Molinier, Chronique normande (1882), pp 190–191. Those checked pages concern military events in 1369; focused whole-volume OCR searches did not locate the cited receipt. The full volume is saved for reproducibility, not offered as proof the payment is fictitious. Source/page miscitation or an OCR miss remains possible. The same modern paragraph calls the king Charles VI in 1370; this chronological error must not be propagated.

The institutional Collégiales notice is marked Fiche à valider. It is useful for a dean succession and archival references, not a substitute for original dated appointments. No kinship to a cardinal or birthplace near Limoges/Toulouse is inferred.
Staise’s office authenticates two different acts, with different notaries and different parties. This does not establish he introduced Charny to Jean du Hem, much less that either made the Shroud.

The expression is erga divinum cultum, toward divine worship. It is not a named endorsement of a Shroud relic. The French act of 20 May and Latin episcopal confirmation of 28 May are distinct documents.
